report.title: Our Water, Our Future: City of Palo Alto 2025 Water Quality Report (City of Palo Alto Utilities 2025 Annual Water Quality Report)

sources_described: Palo Alto's water is delivered by the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS, operated by the SFPUC); the major source is Sierra Nevada snowmelt flowing down the Tuolumne River to Hetch Hetchy Reservoir (unfiltered, UV and chlorine disinfected, pH adjusted, fluoridated and chloraminated), supplemented by local reservoirs in Alameda County treated at the Sunol Valley WTP and San Mateo County reservoirs treated at the Harry Tracy WTP. In 2025 neither the SFRWS upcountry non-Hetch Hetchy sources nor its groundwater wells were used; the SFRWS imported a very small amount (0.38%) of treated water from Santa Clara Valley Water District in April and May.

violations: NOTICE FROM THE SAN FRANCISCO PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION (SFPUC) (p. 4): the SFRWS, operated by the SFPUC, failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant (SVWTP) from June 23, 2025, to July 2, 2025. This monitoring violation was the result of equipment failure (the turbidimeter was not operating) and was corrected on July 3, 2025. The notice states the failure was not an emergency, did not impact water quality, and that during the period the water delivered to Palo Alto customers met all federal and state drinking water standards; operations staff were retrained and additional operational and maintenance activities implemented to prevent recurrence.
extraction_notes: Report covers calendar year 2025 and states Palo Alto's water meets all federal and state drinking water standards (footnote 1: all results met state and federal drinking water health standards). Data tables are on PDF pages 6 ('Your Water Quality Data for 2025': DETECTED CONTAMINANTS and NON-REGULATED WATER QUALITY PARAMETERS) and 7 (CONSTITUENTS WITH SECONDARY STANDARDS and LEAD AND COPPER). There are no per-source columns: all rows are a single SFRWS/SFPUC system column, so source_group is null throughout; turbidity is instead split into rows per treatment source (Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy Water, Filtered Water from SVWTP, Filtered Water from HTWTP), kept in raw_name. The DETECTED CONTAMINANTS table has one combined column 'Average or [Max]': bracketed values are maxima or highest (locational) running annual averages per footnotes 3-4 and are stored with value_basis 'max' or 'highest running annual average' and average=null; unbracketed values are averages. Range lows printed 'ND' or '<x' are stored as 0 with the printed form in notes; averages printed 'ND' or '<2' are stored as null with range high used as value. Copper is printed in ppb (RAL 1300, PHG 300) and lead 90th percentile is printed as 0 although individual samples ranged 0.2 - 9.74 ppb; lead/copper sampling year is 2023 (footnotes 6-7). E. coli printed [0] positive samples is recorded as detected=false. Cryptosporidium is discussed in text only (found at very low levels in source and treated water in 2025, no numbers), so no entry. The report lists no PFAS, radiological or UCMR rows. The PDF was obtained through the WebFetch service because paloalto.gov returns Akamai 403 to direct curl from this host; sha256 is of the saved file.
